title: Testing with JUnit, kotlin.test and the coroutine test utilities

videos.script: Every program in this course so far was checked by running it and reading what it printed. That works once. {{first}} A test is that check written as code, kept beside the program, and run by Gradle every time: two test dependencies, a test block in the build, and a class whose functions are marked test. {{assert}} The assertions kotlin dot test gives you, and the two that return something worth checking: assert fails with, and assert is. {{fails}} A test that fails, and how to read it, because the first question a red test asks is which side is wrong. {{virtual}} Run test, which gives a suspending function somewhere to run and replaces waiting with a clock of its own, so an hour of delay passes in no time at all. {{scheduler}} The test scheduler, which runs nothing until the test says so, and lets a test look at the state between any two steps. {{flows}} And the planner's week model, tested: its failures, and every state a screen would have been shown.
